summary: Approval routing misroutes to shadowed service principal after Okta alias rewrite, blocking interactive console elevation
description:
Issue summary:
Users attempting to request Just-In-Time console elevation for the internal Model Playground are seeing their approvals routed to a service principal (svc-modelbot@redwood.com) instead of the human approver queue. The service principal has an automated deny rule which causes the approval to be rejected immediately, preventing users from getting elevated access.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers across multiple teams unable to perform interactive debugging in model-playground between 2026-03-10T09:05 and ongoing.
- Affects production tenant flows in us-east; has caused interruptions in oncall debugging and slowed down a customer-facing incident response.

Observed behaviour:
- Request is created in approval-service but approver is resolved to svc-modelbot@redwood.com instead of the manager on the access request. Approvals show status "auto-rejected" with audit note: "approver invalid - automation deny".
- Users report UI shows "Pending approval" for ~20s then moves to "Denied" with no notification to the intended manager.

Initial hypothesis:
- Recent Okta group alias rewrite (internal migration of application-owned group identifiers) caused duplication/canonicalization of the SCIM externalId for one service account and a human user. Approval-service currently picks approver using SCIM externalId from the access request claim; duplicate externalId causes routing to the wrong principal.

Why this is high-risk/unique:
- Routing is not falling back to a stable okta.userId or email claim; the dedupe logic in approval-service is brittle for collisions introduced by a mass rename/aliasing operation.

Next steps (planned):
1) Reproduce in staging with migration dataset (in progress).
2) Patch approval-service to prefer okta.userId claim for approver resolution and fall back to email; add monitoring for externalId collisions. (PR drafted: github.com/redwood/platform/pull/4821)
3) Temporary mitigation: manual policy override to route requests to the oncall managers for affected teams.
4) Remediation: run SCIM dedupe migration to ensure externalId uniqueness for human accounts and service principals.

Workaround (customer-impact mitigation):
- Support can manually provision temporary console role to affected users (steps included in comments). Team SRE applied a temporary approval-service feature flag to bypass automated deny rules for requests containing manager@redwood.com as approver (limited window).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to console with an affected human Okta account (post-alias migration)
2) Open Model Playground and request Just-In-Time elevation via the access request flow
3) Observe approval ticket created in approval-service; note approver resolved in ticket metadata
4) Observe the approval routed to svc-modelbot@redwood.com and auto-rejected by automation rules
logs: 2026-03-10T09:06:12Z approval-service INFO create_request id=ar_78321 user=elaine@redwood.com approver_externalId=ext-svc-142
2026-03-10T09:06:13Z approval-service INFO decision auto_rejected id=ar_78321 rule=deny_service_principals audit_note=automation-deny
investigation_notes: Checked Okta SCIM payloads for user and service principal: both entities had externalId 'ext-svc-142' after alias rewrite run on 2026-03-09.
Approval-service resolution logic queried approver by externalId and returned the first match (service principal).
Staging reproduction succeeded when we injected duplicate externalId into staging Okta dataset.
No code change to approval-service for this flow in the last 90 days; root cause is data collision from group/app migration script.
Oncall SRE temporarily toggled 'approval-bypass-automation' feature flag for two teams at 2026-03-10T12:30 to reduce impact while we prepare patch.
current_workaround: Support can grant temporary console elevation via admin console role assignment. Runbook: Confluence page 'approval-service-debug' -> 'Manual elevation steps' (requires Tier-2 admin). SRE has left a temporary feature flag to bypass denies for affected team requests until 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC.
resolution_plan: Short term: promote PR to prefer okta.userId for approver resolution and release hotfix to prod (target 2026-03-13). Long term: run SCIM externalId normalization job and add collision alerts; update migration script to validate uniqueness pre-apply.
comments: Laura Chen (reporter) 2026-03-10: Filing after first customer-impacting support escalations during oncall. Notified security that a service principal appears inappropriately in approver slot.
Diego Alvarez (assignee) 2026-03-10: I reproduced in staging. Drafted hotfix to switch resolution priority to okta.userId. Will open PR for review and coordinate with SRE for rollout window.
SRE-Oncall (channel #incidents) 2026-03-10: Temporary feature flag 'approval-bypass-automation' enabled for teams A and B. Please use manual provisioning for high-risk requests.
Security (2026-03-11): Confirmed no indication of privilege escalation — duplicate externalId is a provisioning bug, not a breach. Recommend full dedupe migration before disabling bypass.
Diego Alvarez 2026-03-12: PR merged to canary; observing normal routing in canary for samples. Preparing prod deploy 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC with rollback plan.
